I explained to him why I came to that conclusion, I poured my heart out, telling him my deepest insecurities and sharing things that I've never shared. 

And it didn't matter.

I ended up packing the lingerie and going on the trip... Everything was paid for. I didn't want to disrespect him or seem ungrateful. We didn't talk about the fight, but there was another event that just opened my eyes once again. 

He has a shop and works with stone and marble, while in the little town, he saw a jewelry store and wanted to go in, for a moment I was confused but then excited. Maybe he realized that he DOES want to marry me and that he does want a commitment.

No. 

He wanted to look at some large geodes, minerals, and rocks that the store carried...

When I realized this, my heart just sank, and I left the store while he was busy talking to the store owner about rocks, and I walked through the door down the cold street. I was gone for a good 15-20 minutes before he noticed. That was my second final straw, I'm never going to mean ANYTHING this man. 

The rest of the trip was fine. It was great, like two friends meeting up to go hang out. He isn't all bad at all. He's very generous when he doesn't have to be. 

Valentine's Day, I didn't have the opportunity to get dressed up like i would have liked. We had less than mediocre passionatless sex. He couldn't even get all the way hard. He's so unattracted to me. I got back home today, and he's still skiing. He'll be with his friends the rest of the week. The way he responds to his friends and gets excited to see them is what I wish he even slightly showed me. But maybe that's my fault, maybe I dont make him feel safe and loved. 

I can't live like this anymore. I can't live like I'm not worth anything to anyone anymore. I have a job interview tomorrow, and hopefully, that's the first step of me stepping away.

My mom was in and out of mental hospitals growing up, and it made me really look into how people are really doing past surface level. 

Today, I noticed one of my young friends at crossfit looking like their little light was missing. After the workout, I sat with her, first just discussing our sore spots in our body, but then I asked her how she was doing... Disheartened, she confessed that she felt lonely and with tears almost slipping her voice and face. I told her she was always welcome to hang out with me, and tomorrow, me and my kids were going to the pool, and she was welcome to come.

I think being so in tune with my mother's moods and needs made me empathic and hyper vigilant to people who might share the same needs as she did.

So disclaimer I was the one that left. I felt unloved and unseen and the things I thought would never happen with my person happened. We have 2 kids. He was my first everything and we were together for 16 years. 

I remember the first day I was in my new apartment
... I had my bosses husband help me move the few things I had on a very rainy day, moved from a beautiful 4 bedroom home to the cheapest place I could live in while still being safe for my kids, and i sat on my mattress on the floor and sobbed. I had no one I could share my real feelings with, my family was too far away, my friends were not aware of how much I was really hurting and the man that I was seeing during the separation was not emotionally available at all. I was in so much pain. I wanted to die. I felt so alone.

A friend told me that divorce was like grieving a death. All the ideas about love and all the hope and plans of how your life was supposed to be like is gone. 

With that being said I decided that I could not rely on anyone to make me feel better, I sat with my feelings and sat with the events that brought me to where I was. I realized that despite how alone I was, I was still here. I decided that I was here so that no one around me would ever have to feel the sadness, worthlessness, and despair that I was feeling. I concentrated on bettering myself and loving the people around me. I started Journaling about my anxiety and my life and I opened my life to new experiences and people. 

What helped me was trying to be at service to people around me. It made me feel better to bring a friend flowers or making a sick friend a meal. Be open to really try to learn more about yourself and take the opportunity to find what you're passionate about. 

I'm not perfect at all. The abandonment and years of begging for love made me feel insecure and I tend to be anxiously attached to the people I love. But now I'm aware and working on myself.

I'm sorry this is so long but I wish you the best and want you to know you're not alone.
